Use the attached user-approved image as the VISUAL STYLE AND PALETTE reference for an original ValStrike tactical FPS environment. Match its architecture/material art direction: pale warm-gray poured concrete, cool gray paving, dark charcoal-blue industrial metal, muted dusty crimson painted accents, occasional faded warm-yellow safety paint and off-white wayfinding marks. Broad clean architectural masses, purposeful bevels, convincing material thickness and restrained edge wear/staining. Premium authored game-environment presentation: grounded construction with readable stylized shapes and controlled detail, exactly the reference's balance. Avoid flat primitive/blockout appearance, voxel/Minecraft geometry, gritty photographic clutter, dense noise, neon sci-fi, saturated multicolor props and excessive rust. Preserve clean sightlines and visual hierarchy. There are NO characters, hands, gloves, weapons or HUD in the output. Do not copy the foreground gun or arms. No text, brands or watermarks.
Create one wide landscape 16:9 EYE-LEVEL environment art example of a connected training-yard courtyard from a different viewpoint than the reference. Show a strong concrete building corner on the left with one large faded diagonal crimson stripe, broad cool-gray paving with expansion seams and a few white/yellow painted guide marks, a dark open service doorway on the right with a shallow warm interior light, an upper catwalk with dark metal uprights and restrained red top rail, and purposeful low concrete cover and modular stacked metal crates in the middle distance. Keep the route clear, believable door and human scale, no decorative clutter filling walkways. Some pale rocky landscape and calm blue sky above the enclosure. Neutral soft afternoon daylight with cool shadows, legible midtones, no dramatic haze. Composition should demonstrate how the wall, paving, barrier and crate material families work together. This is a polished environment concept, not an actual existing level screenshot.

Same material quality as the approved reference, softly lit with contact shadows. Show enough top/side surface to understand construction. Objects are art references, not technical CAD; no dimension arrows, captions or labels. No weapons or ammunition symbols.
